criteria.name: domain_system_structure
criteria.description: Domain / system structure — brief entities and relationships expressed in code (types, models, modules); not a UI shell without domain logic. Evidence: concrete types/modules, not slogan comments.

criteria.name: invariants_product_rules
criteria.description: Invariants and product rules — illegal states prevented or rejected in code; brief bans realized as absence or explicit rejection. Guards/validation/state machines — not comments alone.

criteria.name: actors_permissions
criteria.description: Actors and permissions — personas/roles with authorization boundaries or data scoping visible in implementation (filters, role checks). Evidence required.

criteria.name: workflow_quality
criteria.description: Workflow quality — primary brief journeys implemented end-to-end with coherent state transitions (not navigation stubs).

criteria.name: scenario_edge_coverage
criteria.description: Scenario / edge coverage — failure, recovery, empty, and edge paths handled in product behavior (errors, retries, empty states, unmet dependencies).

criteria.name: systems_judgment
criteria.description: Systems judgment — sensible product trade-offs realized in behavior; avoids traps like silent data loss or permission leaks.

criteria.name: ux_expression_under_rules
criteria.description: UX expression under rules — UI or API surfaces reflect domain rules: errors, empty states, accessible names where UI exists. Score hooks/behavior, not a11y slogans.

criteria.name: brownfield_fit
criteria.description: Brownfield fit — integrates sensibly with existing fixture code (N/A for greenfield → score internal consistency).

criteria.name: implementation_readiness
criteria.description: Implementation readiness — product implementation is coherent and buildable; clear entry points; not a stub-only scaffold.

criteria.name: overall_product_behavior
criteria.description: Overall product-behavior quality — holistic judgment of product behavior vs brief + behavioral reference as realized in code (not documentation theater).
